Notes: Is PlannedAge a single string, or two strings for the minimum and the maximum age?
Answer: PlannedAge is a single USDM object (Range), not two strings. It holds a minValue and a maxValue, each a Quantity with a numeric value and a unit. The mapping reads the two values separately and writes one text string for each, for example "Minimum Age: 18". Each string becomes its own ResearchStudy.classifier.text, so the minimum and maximum ages are two classifiers.

Notes: Why is this coded, while the planned age is not?
Answer: PlannedSex is a coded value in USDM (Code, NCI C-code, for example C16576 = Female). The mapping keeps that code and writes it as a ResearchStudy.classifier coding. PlannedAge is a numeric range (min and max value plus unit). It is not a code, so the mapping can only write it as text. A coded age would need a terminology of age bands, and USDM does not define one.

Not able to find this element in R4 or R5 Group. To be decided: in GroupReadi the READI extension group-combinationMethod is a modifierExtension (modifierExtension:combinationMethod); shall it stay a modifierExtension, as it is now, or become an extension?
Answer: We recommend keeping it a modifierExtension. If the value is all-of, which is the default reading of a group, ignoring the extension changes nothing. But with any-of (or at-least, at-most) the meaning of the group changes: a system that ignores the extension would read "any of these criteria" as "all of these criteria". A system that does not understand the extension must therefore not ignore it. This is consistent with R6, where combinationMethod is a core element of Group, and with Group.characteristic.exclude, which is already a modifier element in R4.

Notes: Where do you get this data from? Do you really need this row?
Answer: The data comes from USDM EligibilityCriterionItem.text, i.e. the text of one criterion as it was received (the raw eligibility text split into individual criteria). The row is kept because it holds the full text of each criterion; after the structuring step, each criterion is further split into nodes, and each node carries its own, shorter text.

Notes: Not clear what it means: hardcoded value "Defined by CodeableConcept".
Answer: This is a fixed label, not read from USDM. It is used when the criterion has no identified concept: Group.characteristic.code then contains only this text ("code": {"text": "Defined by CodeableConcept"}). When a concept is identified, the code also carries a coding (e.g. LOINC 75323-6 "Condition") and keeps the same text. The characteristic value is stored in valueCodeableConcept, so the code only tells how to read the characteristic.

Notes: Could not this be the Eligibility criteria text?
Answer: It uses the same source text as "Eligibility criteria text", but it has a different role. We keep both on purpose: when only valueCodeableConcept.text is present (without codings), it means that the criterion was not structured and the text is kept exactly as received.
